newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche first quarter sales rise 18 percent.
newsitem.headline: Roche first quarter sales rise 18 percent.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG on Tuesday said sales in the first quarter of 1997 rose 18 percent to 4.45 billion Swiss francs with sales of its six top-selling drugs well up.
Adjusting for fluctuating exchange rates, Roche's first quarter sales rose three percent in local currency terms, the company said in a statement ahead of a news conference.
The positive growth pattern seen in 1996 has continued into the first months of 1997 and Roche said it expected to report another good result for this year.
"Barring extraordinary events, we expect to post another good year result for 1997 despite the high levels of investment...for the introduction of new products," Roche said in its 1996 annual report.
Roche last month said 1996 group net profit rose 16 percent to 3.90 billion francs from 3.37 billion in 1995. Group sales rose 10.7 percent to 15.966 billion francs.
The report also said the group anticipated a substantial overall rise in marketing costs due to the launch of new products this year.

During the current year, the company's efforts will be focused on the launch of new products including a cardiovascular agent Posicor, an anti-obesity product named Xenical and a Parkinson's disease treatment called Tasmar.
"The successful launch of these innovative products will require us to significantly expand our sales organisation serving the general practitioner segment," the report said.
"We are thus responding to the increasing importance of ambulatory health care delivery."
Early this year advisory panels in the United States and Europe recommended approval of Posicor for treatment of high blood pressure and angina pectoris.

In the first quarter of this year, U.S. sales of Rivotril/Klonopin, a drug to treat epilepsy, and Toradol, a drug against analgesia, had fallen more sharply than expected due to competition from generic drugs.
Without this decline, global sales for the pharmaceuticals division would have exceeded six percent in local currencies.
Roche sales from its pharma division rose 19 percent in Swiss franc terms to 2.89 billion francs, but in local currencies sales rose three percent.
However, "the growth trend for the division's major established products and new entries remained unchanged", Roche said.
Worldwide sales of Roche's top-selling drugs were well up in the first quarter with Rocephin, Neupogen and Ticlid posting double-digit gains in local currencies.
In the over-the-counter segment of the market, sales were also up by two digit figures in local currencies.
Sales of AIDS drug Invirase rose far ahead of the high growth that had been forecast and sales of CellCept, used in kidney transplants, more than doubled in local currencies.
First quarter sales were well ahead of average growth in important European markets, such as Germany, Italy and Spain as well as Canada and Brazil.
In France, sales were steady in local currency terms, despite government action to curb market growth.
Sales declined slightly in Japan as the market slowed in anticipation of the government-mandated price cut that came into effect on April 1, Roche said.
